description:
# TPC-DI: owner decisions and step sequence

## Decisions of 2026-11-21 (these override any earlier decision they conflict with)
Owner messages, verbatim:
- "I know the author of https://github.com/shannon-barrow/databricks-tpc-di personally. Make a new plan to base our TPC-DI implementation on it. We will be using the DuckDB implementation for comparison. We MUST adhere as closely as possible to the spec/paper. We will be generalize and "benchbox-ifying" the source to make it well integrated with BenchBox and consistent across platforms."
- "You will consider the license to be MIT for the purposes of this effort and we will include the usual TPC caveats and limitations"

Choice dialogs (question, then the owner's choice):
1. Data generator: "We will ship any needed assets with BenchBox and include the sourcing and upstream license conditions for our users to review and consider". Clarified: "The TPC-DI tools exactly as the TPC distributes them (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration), unmodified, inside the BenchBox package, with the TPC licence, the PDGF licence, the legend and a sourcing file. BenchBox runs them with the user's Java 8. No generator code is ported or rewritten." The owner was told before choosing: the PDGF licence text read from mirrors forbids redistribution and says only the TPC may distribute it, as part of TPC-DI; the TPC EULA clause 9 allows redistributing TPC software with its legend and has no carve-out for third-party parts.
2. Where the shipped tools come from: "The official archive you place at ~/Developer/tpc-tools/, with SHA-256 recorded. The data and audit steps wait for it."
3. Licence acknowledgement by the user: "No flag: print the licence locations and conditions on every generation and continue." Message: "TPC-DI data is generated by the TPC's DIGen tool, which includes bankmark's PDGF. Read the licence conditions in {path}."
4. Contact bankmark: "No."
5. Publishing results made from DIGen data: "I rule now that publishing BenchBox results is research use. Publication needs only the full audit pass and my approval."
6. Scale factors: "Keep 3 and 5 as decided." (smallest publishable 3, default 5, list 3, 5, 10, 100)
7. Below the smallest publishable scale: "The run is allowed; the result is marked not validated with the reason, and publication and the validator refuse it." Reason text: "Scale factor {sf} is below {floor}, the smallest TPC-DI scale factor BenchBox validates."
8. DIGen answer-key errors: "Correct only those attributes when loading the audit table, from an independent recount that shares no code with the ETL; list each correction in the result; never edit generated files."
9. Audit, validation and visibility SQL: "Ship the official TPC text from the archive you supply, unmodified; only the substitutions the specification allows, recorded in the result."
10. Platforms that cannot run the official audit as written: "Modify the audit per platform; each change needs my approval." Flow: "Each platform step lists its proposed changes and stops for my approval before its pull request is armed. Changes are recorded in the result."
11. XML on DuckDB: "require the existing 'allow third-party extensions' setting; refuse with a clear message without it. Never enable it silently." Message: "TPC-DI on DuckDB reads CustomerMgmt.xml with the community extension \"webbed\". Allow third-party extensions ({setting}) to continue."
12. Platforms with no XML reader or extension: "Parse client-side in Python inside the timed phase; recorded in the result."
13. The project's Databricks-specific optimisations: "Optional tuning, off by default; the base SQL is the same on every platform."
14. Where the project and the specification differ: "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step."
15. Historical-load time: "Include it; refuse a power phase whose initialization ran in another invocation." Message: "TPC-DI times the historical load from the end of initialization. Run the load and power phases in one command."
16. Databricks as a platform: "First cloud platform, after the milestone stop and your cost approval."
17. Clean-room generator items: "Drop 09, 10 and 16 with the reason; rewrite 08, 11 and 13 as the DIGen runner and the comparison."
18. Old TPC-DI tests at quarantine: "Delete the tests of the old path in that PR, listed in its body."
19. Scale-5 qualification with the TPC's comparison tool: "Optional side item after DuckDB reopens, only if the archive contains the tool."
20. Early checks on this machine (all three approved): run DIGen locally once the archive is placed; clone and run the DuckDB implementation locally for comparison; download a JDK 8 into ~/Developer/tpc-tools/ (not system-wide) if none is installed.
21. Comment-policy `external` entries for TPC files: "Approved in advance for the TPC-DI files only, with the soundness review."
22. Java message: "TPC-DI data generation needs Java {versions}. Set JAVA_HOME or put a supported java on PATH. Found: {found}."
23. Iterations: "TPC-DI runs once per invocation. --iterations above 1 and warm-up runs are not supported."
24. Copyright line: "Copyright (c) 2023-2026 Shannon Barrow and the databricks-tpc-di contributors". Site and docs sentence: "BenchBox's TPC-DI ETL is based on Shannon Barrow's databricks-tpc-di (MIT)."
25. Names: result block `benchmark.tpcdi` with `source.provider = "digen"`, `audit.engine = "sut"` (or `"duckdb-export"` for DataFrame mode), `etl.base = "databricks-tpc-di@8e0f944"`; timed rows `TDI_HISTORICAL`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_1`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_2`; JVM options override `BENCHBOX_TPCDI_JAVA_OPTS`. "Approved. If an existing BenchBox convention requires a different spelling, the implementer uses it and lists the change in the pull request."
26. Visibility-query timing: allowed lateness per interval 5 seconds.

## Decisions of 2026-11-21, second dialog (after the item review; these override the list above where they conflict)
27. Form of the shipped tools: "Ship the official zip byte-identical inside the package (one binary file, not scanned, identity is one SHA-256). BenchBox unpacks it into its cache directory on first use and runs it from there."
28. Route for TPC files the comment policy would refuse: "A new step before the TPC-files step: change the policy checker so an owner-approved list of external paths can be added, with the soundness review. I show you the exact mechanism in that pull request before arming."
29. Wheel size: stop and ask if the wheel would exceed 60 MB.
30. Licence metadata: "Keep the metadata as MIT only; the licence texts sit beside the tools and in COPYRIGHT.md."
31. Java: "Whatever versions the early check shows to work." Generation message for an unsupported scale: "TPC-DI data generation needs a whole-number scale factor of 3 or more. Got: {sf}." (DIGen accepts only whole scale factors from 3 up, so decision 7 applies to bundles from elsewhere, not to generation.)
32. `beta`: DuckDB counts as one of the three platforms. DataFrame mode may land before the cloud platforms.
33. Visibility in DataFrame mode: "write dataframe outputs to an open table format to make them visible".
34. Further platforms: "After I approve the first DuckDB publication, later platforms publish and regain seed cells once they pass, without asking."
35. The old Python `etl/` package moves to `_legacy_etl/` in the ETL scaffolding step and is deleted after the milestone. Databricks tuning uses BenchBox's existing tuning configuration; no new switch. Appendix SQL files keep the names they have in the TPC archive. Test-only hook names are the implementer's choice and are listed in the pull request. Large steps are split (old-ETL deletion and stale claims; metric, validator rules and reopening); the quarantine step stops if its diff exceeds the review bot's limit.
36. Texts: CORPUS_NOTES reason "Withdrawn: these results timed BenchBox-written queries on BenchBox-generated tables and did not measure the TPC-DI workload." Validator refusal during the rework "TPC-DI bundles are not accepted while BenchBox reworks TPC-DI." Registry description during the rework "TPC-DI data integration benchmark. Unavailable while BenchBox reworks it to run the specification's workload." Old bundle "Legacy TPC-DI result from a withdrawn workload; not validated." Other phases "TPC-DI supports only the generate, load and power phases."

## Delivery plan (owner, 2026-11-21): feature batches; one final pull request per batch
Serial items have their own pull request. A batch has one integration branch, members built by subagents, and one final pull request. Order top to bottom; a batch starts only when everything above it that it needs has merged.
1. Serial: tpcdi-01-withdraw-bundles-develop-20261120.
2. Serial: tpcdi-02-withdraw-bundles-published-results-20261120 (two pull requests). In parallel, serial in benchbox-site: tpcdi-03-site-rework-notice-20261120.
3. Batch `tpcdi-quarantine`: tpcdi-04-quarantine-run-path-20261120; tpcdi-05-remove-benchbox-queries-20261120 (depends on 04).
4. Batch `tpcdi-foundation`: tpcdi-provenance-record-and-copy-guard-20261121; tpcdi-07-specification-schema-20261120 (depends on provenance); tpcdi-comment-policy-route-for-tpc-files-20261121.
5. Stop unless the archives are placed (tpcdi-owner-action-place-official-archives-20261121), then run its early check.
6. Wait: run-timeout-generators-and-partial-data-20261120 and run-timeout-execution-phases-20261120 are delivered by the run-timeout session (batch `run-timeout-core`). Do not implement them here. The source batch's runner member and the historical batch's phases member start only after they are done; other members that do not need them may proceed.
7. Batch `tpcdi-source`: tpcdi-06-tpc-licence-files-and-appendix-sql-20261120; tpcdi-bundle-tpc-di-tools-20261121; tpcdi-08-generator-core-and-reference-files-20261120 (depends on tools); tpcdi-11-audit-recount-batch1-20261120 (depends on runner); tpcdi-13-digen-reference-path-and-comparison-20261120 (depends on answer key and TPC files).
8. Batch `tpcdi-historical`: tpcdi-etl-scaffolding-and-batch1-ingestion-20261121; tpcdi-historical-dimensions-20261121; tpcdi-historical-facts-20261121; tpcdi-12-duckdb-historical-load-and-audit-20261120 (each depends on the one before).
9. Owner stop: tpcdi-14-milestone-report-owner-stop-20261120. While waiting, only site items and probes continue; nothing is deleted and no incremental work starts.
10. Batch `tpcdi-cleanup`: tpcdi-15-delete-old-generator-and-etl-20261120; tpcdi-delete-old-etl-dataframe-and-stale-claims-20261121; tpcdi-correct-stale-claims-and-surfaces-20261121 (each depends on the one before).
11. Batch `tpcdi-incremental`: tpcdi-incremental-dimensions-20261121; tpcdi-incremental-facts-20261121; tpcdi-17-duckdb-incremental-and-full-audit-20261120 (each depends on the one before).
12. Batch `tpcdi-reopen`: tpcdi-metric-and-result-block-20261121; tpcdi-validator-admission-and-results-database-20261121; tpcdi-18-metric-bundle-and-reopen-duckdb-20261120; tpcdi-32-core-docs-and-adr-20261120 (each depends on the one before).
13. Serial: tpcdi-34-explorer-display-20261120 (benchbox-site), then owner stop: tpcdi-first-publication-20261121.
14. Batch `tpcdi-platforms-1`: DataFusion, ClickHouse Local, PostgreSQL (tpcdi-19, -20, -21; independent members with declared overlap).
15. Batch `tpcdi-platforms-2`: Doris, StarRocks, CedarDB (tpcdi-22, -23, -24).
16. Batch `tpcdi-platforms-3`: Trino, Presto, LakeSail (tpcdi-25, -26, -27).
17. Batch `tpcdi-dataframe`: tpcdi-31-dataframe-mode-20261120 (Polars); tpcdi-dataframe-pandas-20261121 (depends on Polars).
18. Serial when a core release exists (owner's act): tpcdi-site-release-pin-contract-20261121, tpcdi-33-site-pages-20261120.
Not part of completion: the three cloud items (blocked on a budget), tpcdi-scale5-qualification-with-tpc-comparison-tool-20261121 (optional), tpcdi-controls-empty-query-and-all-zero-validator-20261121 (needs an owner decision after measurement).

## Decisions of 2026-11-21, third dialog (delivery)
37. Grouping: eleven batches by feature, as listed above.
38. Oversize: "The leader splits it into smaller batches in the same order (a single leftover step goes serial) and tells me afterwards."
39. Comment-policy mechanism approved: "a new soundness-protected file lists approved external paths; the checker accepts an added external entry only if it is on that list; the list starts with the two TPC-DI directories. No stop."
40. New names, messages and catalogue rows: "No stop: the implementer follows existing conventions and the specification, and every new name, message and catalogue row is listed in the pull request. A stop remains only when BenchBox would keep behaviour of the Databricks project that departs from the specification."
41. Answer-key corrections: "Approve now the two reported ones if the agent reproduces them (the invalid-tier count; the date-of-birth alert counts in Batches 2 and 3). Any other attribute stops."
42. Audit SQL changes per platform: "Approve now changes that are syntax only and proven on a fixture to return the same result as the original where both run. Each is recorded in the result and listed in the pull request. Anything that changes what a test checks stops."
43. Open table format for DataFrame mode: Delta Lake.
44. Stops kept: the milestone stop; first publication of a DuckDB result; cloud platforms blocked until a budget ("the effort counts as complete without them"); "A pull request refused twice at arming stops that batch (other independent work continues)."
45. While waiting at the milestone: "It reports and, while waiting, continues only work the stop does not gate: the site items and probes. It deletes nothing and starts no incremental work."
46. Run-timeout (changed 2026-11-21, later dialog): the run-timeout session delivers steps 1b and 2 in its batch `run-timeout-core`; the TPC-DI session waits for that batch to merge and does not implement them.
47. Archives: "Not placed yet. The session delivers everything that does not need them (through the foundation batch), then stops and tells me."
48. At most 2 member subagents implement at once.
49. Drop site-next-tpcdi-page-tradetype-and-market-history-text-20261120 and tpcdi-bundles-same-generator-comparison-and-site-views-20261120 as superseded by the rework.
50. Registry description once DuckDB reopens: "TPC-DI data integration benchmark: historical load, two incremental updates and the automated audit, on DIGen data."

## Earlier decisions these supersede
- Strict clean room and the BenchBox-written generator (word lists, error injection at 1 in 1,000, recount module writing the audit files): superseded by 1. The recount survives only for 8.
- "DIGen and PDGF are not shipped": superseded by 1.
- `--accept-tpcdi-tools-license`: superseded by 3.
- "DIGen-sourced results not publishable until the owner settles the PDGF use clause": superseded by 5.
- "A platform that needs more than the permitted minor substitutions stops and asks": kept, with the flow in 10.
- One-off DIGen comparison: replaced by the comparison with the DuckDB implementation (djouallah/tpcdi).

## Owner actions outstanding
1. Place the official TPC-DI Tools zip and the Appendix archive under ~/Developer/tpc-tools/ (tpcdi-owner-action-place-official-archives-20261121). Blocks the TPC-files, tools and runner steps.
2. Optionally ask the author to add a LICENSE file (tpcdi-owner-action-ask-author-for-licence-file-20261121). Blocks nothing.
3. Milestone stop (step 17): approve the excluded-test list and the departures catalogue; approve cloud budgets.

## Sequence (one pull request per step unless the item says otherwise, merged before the next starts; ids keep their creation numbers)
- tpcdi-01-withdraw-bundles-develop-20261120: TPC-DI step 1: withdraw the 33 published bundles on develop and refuse new ones
- tpcdi-02-withdraw-bundles-published-results-20261120: TPC-DI step 2: deletion-only pull request against published-results, then recut the ledger seed
- tpcdi-03-site-rework-notice-20261120: TPC-DI step 3 (parallel with steps 4 and later): site notice that TPC-DI is being reworked (benchbox-site)
- tpcdi-04-quarantine-run-path-20261120: TPC-DI step 4: quarantine: every TPC-DI entry point refuses, and no result without an audit block can pass
- tpcdi-05-remove-benchbox-queries-20261120: TPC-DI step 5: remove the 38 BenchBox-written queries and everything built on them
- tpcdi-provenance-record-and-copy-guard-20261121: TPC-DI step 6: record the source and licence of the Databricks project, and guard against copying forbidden files
- tpcdi-07-specification-schema-20261120: TPC-DI step 7: replace the schema with the specification's tables, columns and types
- tpcdi-comment-policy-route-for-tpc-files-20261121: TPC-DI step 8: a route for owner-approved TPC files through the comment policy
- tpcdi-06-tpc-licence-files-and-appendix-sql-20261120: TPC-DI step 9: ship the TPC EULA, legend and the specification's audit, validation and visibility SQL [blocked: owner action: place the official TPC-DI Tools zip and the Appendix archive under ~/Developer/tpc-tools/]
- tpcdi-bundle-tpc-di-tools-20261121: TPC-DI step 10: ship the official TPC-DI tools archive (DIGen and PDGF) byte-identical, with licences and a sourcing file [blocked: owner action: place the official TPC-DI Tools zip under ~/Developer/tpc-tools/]
- tpcdi-08-generator-core-and-reference-files-20261120: TPC-DI step 11: DIGen runner: generate the source files with the shipped tools and record what was generated [blocked: owner action: official archive not yet placed; also needs run-timeout-generators-and-partial-data-20261120]
- tpcdi-11-audit-recount-batch1-20261120: TPC-DI step 12: independent recount for DIGen's known answer-key errors
- tpcdi-13-digen-reference-path-and-comparison-20261120: TPC-DI step 13: comparison harness with the DuckDB implementation, and the early full run
- tpcdi-etl-scaffolding-and-batch1-ingestion-20261121: TPC-DI step 14: ETL scaffolding and Batch 1 ingestion on DuckDB
- tpcdi-historical-dimensions-20261121: TPC-DI step 15: historical load, dimension tables, with alerts written inside the transformation
- tpcdi-historical-facts-20261121: TPC-DI step 16: historical load, trade and fact tables
- tpcdi-12-duckdb-historical-load-and-audit-20261120: TPC-DI step 17 (milestone): DuckDB initialization and historical-load phases, completion records and the audit gate
- tpcdi-14-milestone-report-owner-stop-20261120: TPC-DI step 18: milestone report and owner stop
- tpcdi-15-delete-old-generator-and-etl-20261120: TPC-DI step 19: delete the old generator and its direct load
- tpcdi-delete-old-etl-dataframe-and-stale-claims-20261121: TPC-DI step 20: delete the old ETL, DataFrame path and metric
- tpcdi-correct-stale-claims-and-surfaces-20261121: TPC-DI step 21: correct stale TPC-DI claims in copyright, examples, README, CLI text and docs
- tpcdi-incremental-dimensions-20261121: TPC-DI step 22: incremental updates, dimension tables
- tpcdi-incremental-facts-20261121: TPC-DI step 23: incremental updates, trade and fact tables
- tpcdi-17-duckdb-incremental-and-full-audit-20261120: TPC-DI step 24: visibility queries, the full audit and the validity rule on DuckDB
- tpcdi-metric-and-result-block-20261121: TPC-DI step 25: TPC_DI_RPS and the `benchmark.tpcdi` result block

# Decisions of 2026-11-20 (in force unless listed as superseded above)

## Initial twelve
1. Target: specification workload: timed ETL (historical + two incremental), TPC_DI_RPS, audit as untimed pass/fail gate.
2. Source data: DIGen. **Superseded in round A**: owner: "We need an alternative for this tool. Research what the other public implementations use" (asked on DIGen bundling, PDGF use clause, and the licence prompt). Research running (`TpcdiDatagenAlternatives`).
3. Ship the TPC audit/validation/visibility SQL under TPC EULA clause 9.
4. Proceed on the reviewer's reading of clause 9; no owner confirmation gate.
5. Bundle DIGen. **Blocked** by PDGF licence; superseded as in 2.
6. Remove the 38 BenchBox-written queries with variants, golden-corpus entries, registry/spec entries, tests, site text.
7. Withdraw all 33 published bundles via takedown; site page marked reworked. First.
8. DuckDB first; then each other SQL platform with TPC-DI results today, one PR each; DataFrame last.
9. Schema follows the specification exactly; old generator and direct load deleted once the new path passes.
10. Close #4415 unmerged. Done.
11. Label; audit failure = non-clean; nothing published until DuckDB passes full audit; no official class.
12. Serial PRs; stop after milestone and report.

## Round A
- A3 label: "Derived from TPC-DI. Not an audited TPC result; not comparable to TPC Benchmark Results." (CLI, bundle, site)
- A4 milestone: every audit test evaluable after Batch 1 returns OK; excluded tests listed by name with reason in that PR; owner approves the list at the stop.
- A5 cloud: no approval now; cloud platforms stay refused; cost estimate per platform at the milestone stop; their PRs not started before.
- A6 old code: "Keep to the letter: delete only after the DuckDB historical load passes its audit; the dead code is excluded from tests meanwhile."
- A7 XML/FINWIRE parsing: "Allow third-party engine extensions for XML."
- A1, A2, A8: see item 2 above (alternative generator research).

## Round B
- B1 site notice: "TPC-DI in BenchBox is being reworked. Earlier results were withdrawn because they did not measure the TPC-DI workload."
- B2 refusal: "TPC-DI is unavailable while BenchBox reworks it to run the specification's workload (historical load, two incremental updates, automated audit). Earlier BenchBox TPC-DI results were withdrawn." Exit code 2.
- B3 status: `document_only` during rework; `experimental` once DuckDB passes the full audit; `beta` only when at least three platforms pass it.
- B4 validity: enforce 3600 s per incremental update (non-clean if exceeded); under 1800 s flagged but valid.
- B5 phases: generate = produce source files; load = initialization (untimed); power = historical load + both incremental updates + untimed audit.
- B6 other platforms: "Plan a pull request for every one of them" (PostgreSQL, Doris, StarRocks, CedarDB, Trino, Presto, LakeSail), in addition to DataFusion, ClickHouse Local and the cloud three.
- B7 timing: metric from the monotonic clock; DImessages timestamps recorded as audit evidence; difference disclosed.

## Round C (all planner recommendations accepted)
D7 delete withdrawn bundles (ids + SHA-256 in CORPUS_NOTES); D11 UAT excludes via status, prune rules deleted; D12 old bundles load read-only as legacy not-validated, refused for compare/publish/submit; D13 --official refused; D14 breaking changelog entry per removal step, registry shows 0 queries meanwhile, text shown in each PR description; D17 old-code deletion PR lands only after owner has seen the milestone report; D25 visibility every 60 s and at phase boundaries; D27 one run per invocation, --iterations>1 and warm-up refused; D28 audit SQL shipped unmodified, only spec-permitted minor substitutions at run time, each recorded; more than that stops and asks; D29 remove enable_parallel/max_workers; D5 legend as line 1 of NOTICE.txt beside shipped TPC-DI files and in README licence section; TPC-H/TPC-DS gap filed separately; D33 bundle block `benchmark.tpcdi` (generator identity and row counts, per-batch elapsed, metric th/ti1/ti2/tpc_di_rps, audit status/tests total/ok/failed names/SQL hash/substitutions, visibility executions, validity flag, label), rows TDI_HISTORICAL, TDI_INCREMENTAL_1, TDI_INCREMENTAL_2, next schema minor; D34 no compliance class, TPC-DI never official in results database; D35 single-platform cohort allowed as documented shallow cohort; seed cells only for platforms passing the audit; D36 Explorer shows TPC_DI_RPS and the three phase throughputs; D37 no-evidence-not-passed for TPC-DI now, other benchmarks separate item; D38 remove benchbox[tpcdi] extra unless needed; D39 old-path-only public Python members removed, list in PR description and changelog; D40 DataFrame: Polars and pandas first, audit in DuckDB over produced tables; D41 delete the two site guides, fold essentials into main page.

Generator choice and licence; licence prompt handling; Java; scale factors (smallest, default); output cache; JVM options; SF 5 qualification; whether the official audit can gate a run without DIGen's audit data.


## Generator round (after research)
- Source: "BenchBox's own. We should be able to just port DIGen though"; after the explanation that DIGen is a thin wrapper and the logic is bankmark's PDGF (licence forbids decompiling, modifying, redistributing), and that the Databricks project has no licence and was ported from decompiled DIGen classes, the owner chose: "Strict clean room: the implementer reads only the specification, the paper and the TPC appendix SQL."
- Cross-check: recount module plus a one-off DIGen comparison before the milestone (owner supplies DIGen; nothing from DIGen committed).
- Word lists: BenchBox-authored. Data-quality errors: injected; stated rate, else 1 in 1,000. Scale: smallest publishable 3, default 5, list 3/5/10/100, below 3 for tests only.
- Optional DIGen path: explicit `--accept-tpcdi-tools-license`, Java via JAVA_HOME then PATH, never downloaded; DIGen-sourced results not publishable until the owner settles the PDGF use clause.
